rows.evidence: AssertionError: kind WRITE_TIMEOUT at 1162 ms; the backend (receive buffer 4096 bytes) had read 3840 bytes in its slow phase, the last at 1101 ms; the last 1 KiB pieces the proxy socket accepted completed at [14, 14, 14, 14, 15, ...] ms expected:<200> but was:<504>
rows.note: Dropped: the premise (progress during the timed-out write) is false. A 1 KiB-splitting probe on the proxy's plain socket shows the socket accepted no byte from ~15 ms to the 1 s deadline; the backend's reads came from its own receive buffer and TCP opened no window. The write was blocked without progress, so WRITE_TIMEOUT matches PRD-109 and the Implementation Notes (deadline per socket write).
504 page of a ProxyException with a wrapped cause, a cause-level suppressed exception and a top-level suppressed exception (all naming host and port) names neither; the cause class stays.
A RuntimeException and a non-proxy HttpException(502, null, UnknownHostException) keep the plain printStackTrace page with cause messages.
A TCP connect that hangs until its socket is closed (default 10 s connect timeout, total 1 s) gives 504 TOTAL_TIMEOUT after about 1 s, not 502 CONNECT_FAILED.
After a 256 KiB body written through per-write deadlines and a READ_TIMEOUT, the JVM-wide deadline scheduler queue is empty when onError runs (no leaked write or total deadline task).
A total deadline that fires after the final check (res.status stalled 1.5 s on a 1 s total) aborts the client connection, logs one TOTAL_TIMEOUT, calls no onError and returns the slot.
Content-Length variant of AC-12 (copyLength path): 504 TOTAL_TIMEOUT with exactly one client body read after the deadline.
https variant: 64 MiB body to a TLS backend that never reads gives 504 WRITE_TIMEOUT in about 1 s (plain socket closed under TLS). TLS watchdog executor properties are wave-19 and were not tested.
https variant: SO_TIMEOUT set on the SSL socket reaches the plain socket; 504 READ_TIMEOUT after about 1 s.
